questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
It prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.
It prevents the vehicle from going too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To test the trailer brakes.
To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To speed up the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only when testing the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: If the trailer drifts while you are backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction the trailer is drifting.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction the trailer is drifting.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it right away by turning the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve protect?

options.text: It ensures the engine gets enough oil.
It prevents the truck from going too fast.
It keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When pulling trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Avoid making sudden movements.
Press the accelerator hard when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden movements.
questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering movements can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: Are fully-loaded rigs more or less likely to roll over than empty rigs?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They are just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over than empty rigs. The weight of the cargo raises the center of gravity, increasing rollover risk.

questions.question: Can you use the trailer hand valve for parking?

options.text: Yes, always use it for parking.
Use it only for parking on downhill slopes.
No, never use it for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never use it for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It may release the brake system's air pressure, which releases the brakes holding the vehicle. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: If you are unsure about your path while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Continue backing.
Stop and get out to look.
Continue backing slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure of your path while backing, stop the vehicle, get out, and check your path of travel.

questions.question: How should cargo be loaded to prevent a rollover?

options.text: With most weight on the driver's side of the trailer.
Near the rear of the trailer.
Evenly spread throughout the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Evenly spread throughout the trailer.
questions.explanation: Distribute cargo weight evenly throughout the trailer to reduce rollover risk. Do not place too much weight on one side of the trailer.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
They are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: Before you start driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that air reaches all brakes on all trailers. Open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves and listen for air escaping. Close both valves before you drive.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need extra space on the road because they:

options.text: Drive slower than other commercial vehicles.
Are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more room to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles. Managing space correctly is very important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: When glad hands are coupled, the seals should be pressed together at a ____ angle.

options.text: 50-degree
180-degree
90-degree

questions.correctAnswerText: 90-degree
questions.explanation: Make sure you couple the correct glad hands together. When they are connected, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, you must first turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
To the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing without a trailer, turn the vehicle in the direction you want to go. When backing with a trailer, start by turning in the opposite direction. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you couple correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling or uncoupling of combination vehicles can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This is more noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color shows service lines?

options.text: White
Yellow
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers couple glad hands correctly. Blue shows service lines and red shows emergency lines.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The trailer will have no brakes.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply in the trailer's air tank leaks away, the brakes will not work and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that limits the amount of cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar. It is used to control the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving could cause a skid.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color shows emergency or supply lines?

options.text: White
Yellow
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers couple glad hands correctly. Blue shows service lines and red shows emergency lines.
